front: Encoding vs. formatting on the Marks card
back: Dropping a field on Color, Size or Shape encodes data and creates a legend. Clicking them without a field formats every mark the same way, with no legend.

front: Categorical palette
back: What Tableau uses when a discrete field (typically a dimension) is on Color: a distinct colour and a legend entry per member.

front: Quantitative legend
back: What Tableau shows when a continuous field (typically a measure) is on Color: a continuous range of colours.

front: How do you change colours on the Marks card?
back: On the Marks card, click Color > Edit Colors. You can also use Edit Colors from the colour legend's menu.

front: Change colours for a discrete field
back: Select a member and pick a colour, or choose a palette and click Assign Palette.

front: Color options only for a continuous field
back: Sequential or diverging palettes, Stepped Color (groups values into uniform bins), Reversed, and Use Full Color Range with a diverging palette.

front: Default colour of marks, and how to recolour all marks without a field
back: Blue for most marks, black for text. On the Marks card, click Color and select a colour from the menu.

front: Opacity, borders and halos (Color menu)
back: Opacity sets transparency. Marks have no border by default. Halos are available only with a background image or map.

front: How do you set one font for the whole workbook?
back: On the Format menu, select Workbook. The Format Workbook pane replaces the Data pane.

front: How do you change the font of one sheet?
back: From the Format menu, choose the part of the view you want, such as Font, Borders or Filters.

front: Exam trap: workbook vs. worksheet fonts
back: Format > Workbook changes fonts everywhere and overwrites sheet-level font changes. Format > Font changes only the current sheet's pane and header text.

front: What does Reset to Defaults do in the Format Workbook pane?
back: It undoes the workbook-level font changes.

front: What font settings can you set for a view's pane text or header text?
back: The font, style, size and color, for either the pane text or the header text, or both.

front: How do you put shapes on marks?
back: Set the mark type to Shape, then drag a field to Shape on the Marks card.

front: What happens with a dimension on Shape?
back: Tableau separates the marks by member and assigns a unique shape to each member.

front: What happens with a measure on Shape?
back: The measure is converted to a discrete measure.

front: How many default shapes are there before they repeat?
back: Ten unique shapes. With more than 10 members, the shapes repeat.

front: How do you pick different shapes?
back: Click Shape on the Marks card, or select Edit Shape on the legend's card menu.

front: How do you add custom shapes?
back: Copy image files (.png, .gif, .jpg, .bmp or .tiff) into a new folder in My Tableau Repository\Shapes. The folder name becomes the palette name. Click Reload Shapes if Tableau was running.

front: Exam trap: shapes on the Marks card do not show
back: Shapes only show with the Shape mark type.

front: Where do you turn on viz animations?
back: Choose Format > Animations. Under Workbook Default, click On to animate every sheet.

front: Animation Duration
back: Choose a preset or specify a custom duration of up to 10 seconds.

front: Animation style: Simultaneous vs. Sequential
back: Simultaneous plays all animations at once and is faster. Sequential fades out marks, moves and sorts them, then fades them in, which is easier to follow.

front: How do you override animations for one sheet?
back: Change the settings under Selected Sheet in Format > Animations. Reset All Sheets returns every sheet to the workbook default.

front: How do you change the size of all marks?
back: On the Marks card, click Size and move the slider left or right. The size of your data view is not modified.

front: What does a continuous field on Size do?
back: The smallest value gets the smallest mark and the largest value the largest mark. A discrete field gets a unique size per member.

front: Where do you edit sizes for a field on Size?
back: Use Edit Sizes from the size legend's menu. Sizes vary Automatically, By range or From zero, and Reversed gives the biggest mark to the smallest value.

front: How do you give bars a fixed width?
back: Click Size, choose Fixed and enter the Width in axis units (in days on a continuous date axis).

front: When does a legend appear?
back: When you add fields to Color, Size and Shape on the Marks card. The legend shows how the view is encoded.

front: Does formatting a mark without a field create a legend?
back: No. With one colour or one size there is nothing to explain.

front: Why hide a legend, and why show it again?
back: Hide it when the encoding is obvious, for example when the members are labelled on the marks. Show it when readers need the key.

front: Legend card menu
back: Each legend card has its own menu, which also holds Edit Colors, Edit Shape or Edit Sizes.

front: Exam trap: which palette type follows from continuity?
back: A discrete field on Color gets a categorical palette. A continuous field gets a sequential or diverging gradient.
